text: Reading 200,000 bytes one at a time took 43 ms unbuffered and 3 ms buffered. Where did the cost go?
choices: The buffered version reads ahead on a background thread, overlapping I/O with computation.
Buffering lets the JIT inline the read loop, which it cannot do across a stream boundary.
Each unbuffered read is a system call; a buffer turns 200,000 of them into about 25 refills plus array accesses.
The unbuffered version reads the physical disk each time while the buffered one uses the OS cache.
explanation: A system call is a transition into the kernel and back, costing a few hundred nanoseconds regardless of how much data crosses it — about 215 ns each here, essentially all overhead, since the data was in the OS cache the whole time. The general form recurs everywhere: batch the expensive operation. Cache lines, `ArrayList` growth, database round trips and network packets are all this.
